summary: Dune: Imperium – Uprising is a standalone expansion/sequel that keeps the same worker-placement-plus-deckbuilding core but adds new mechanisms like sandworm riding, spy networks, and contracts for extra strategic texture. It supports up to 6 players with a new team mode, making it feel like a bigger, richer version of the original rather than a wholly new game.
praised: Adds meaningful new strategic layers (spies, sandworms, contracts) without bloating the core
Compatible with base game and other expansions for mix-and-match variety
criticised: Slightly higher complexity and longer setup than the base game
Some new mechanics can feel like they dilute the tight original design
Best experienced after already knowing the base game
Team mode can be uneven depending on group experience

interaction.kind: Worker placement contention and area conflict
interaction.detail: As in the base game, players contend for placement spots and battle over a shared combat track, with new elements like sandworms and spy actions adding extra ways to interfere with opponents. Team mode adds a shared victory state between two players against another pair.

scoring.how_you_win: As in the base game, you build Victory Points through Conflict victories and Faction influence/alliances, with the added twist that winning a Conflict whose battle icon matches a card in your supply also scores a VP; the game ends at the close of a round in which a player has 10+ VP, or when the Conflict deck is exhausted, and the player with the most VP wins (ties broken by spice, solari, water, then troops).
